header.title: The Angel Metatron (Chanoch): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Otzar Midrashim
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:rabbinic:metatron:eisenstein, from Eisenstein's Otzar Midrashim (New York, 1915), in Sefaria's export (public domain), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY 4.0: credit Eisenstein's Otzar Midrashim (New York, 1915), in Sefaria's export (the source's own licence is public domain) and this AI translation.

notes.2.1.4: The parentheses (the gloss on the 'first ones', Yalkut Reuveni, 'ibid.', Tziyyoni) are the editor's and are translated as they stand; Hakham ha-Razim, the source cited there, is left as a name. 2.1.4: 'Youth' is נער, Metatron's title; 'assigned' renders זיווגני, literally 'paired/matched me'. 2.1.5: the angels' words could also be read as a statement ('the first ones did not speak well'), and the closing עוד 'any more' is awkward. '[rebelliously]' is the edition's bracketed סרה. 'Three hundred and sixty-five thousand [times] the orb of the sun' renders a compressed phrase, על שס״ה אלפים בגלגל חמה. 'To the measure of a thousand parasangs' may give the size of each idol or their extent. The enosh/adam remark plays on אנוש 'man' and Enosh. 2.1.6: 'one thousand three hundred thousand gates of wisdom' stands as written, perhaps a corruption of 300,000. שמ״א is read as an abbreviation of שלש מאות אלף, 300,000, matching the figure before it; as a numeral it would be 341. 'Prince of the World' (שר עולם) attaches loosely and may be displaced. The comma after מפני may mean the command ends 'before Me'; rendered as 'for'. 'Every kind of' (כל מעין של) could also be 'every spring of'. 2.1.7: 'the Lesser YHWH' is הוי״ה הקטן, a substitute spelling of the divine name. 'Face within face' (פנים בפנים) is obscure. 'Light of glory that are on my head': no crown is named here. 'The splendour of the height of all' (הדר מרום כל) is an obscure epithet. The princes' names are formed on what each governs; Zikiel's זיקים may be sparks or comets.
notes.3.5: Afafniel is written אפפניא״ל; the explanation ties the name to the ophanim, so it probably stands for Ofanniel. YHWH joined to the princes' names (Afafniel, Serafiel, Dabriel) is part of the name and is not rendered 'the LORD'. The parenthesis on the eye count is the editor's; 'sixteen on each side' does not fit 2,191 per side and may belong to the faces. Several of Afafniel's duties are obscure and rendered literally: מפחד 'awes' (perhaps for מפאר 'glorifies'), מקהיל את דוכנם 'assembles their platform', מרוה את פנתם 'waters their corner'. '[like] the orb of the sun' supplies a comparison the text lacks. Zadkael (צדקאל) appears abruptly, as if from another passage. נוגה is rendered Venus, though it can mean simply 'brightness'. 3.6: 'one prince' reads שר for the text's צד 'side'. כנחלים 'like streams' may be a slip for כגחלים 'like coals'. 'Stars of lightning' (כוכבי הברק) is unclear. Damuel (דמואל), prince of Persia, I cannot identify. 'Book-chests' renders דלוסקות. 'Choirs' (שירות) may stand for שורות 'rows'. The seraphim are named from שורפין 'burn', and Dabriel from דבור 'word'.

nodes.text: Rabbi Ishmael said: At that hour the youths of the chariot, the *ophanim* [wheels] of flame and the seraphim of consuming fire came and asked, ‘From what people is he? From what tribe is he? What is the nature of this one?’ Metatron answered them and said to them, ‘From the people of Israel, chosen by the Holy One, blessed be He, to be His people; from the tribe of Levi he is, which is lifted up to His name; from the seed of Aaron he is, whom He chose for Himself as a minister, on whom the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself bound the crown of priesthood at Sinai.’ At once they opened [their mouths] and said, ‘Surely this one is worthy to gaze upon the chariot, as it is written, Happy is the people that is so placed.’ Rabbi Ishmael said: At that hour I asked Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence; I said to him, ‘What is your name?’ He said to me, ‘I have seventy names, corresponding to the seventy languages that are in the world, and all of them are after the name of the King of the kings of kings; but my King calls me Youth.’ Rabbi Ishmael said: I said to Metatron, ‘Why are you called by the name of your Creator with seventy names, and you are greater than all the princes, higher than all the angels, more beloved than all the ministers, more honoured than all the hosts and greater than all the mighty ones in kingship, in greatness and in glory — why then do they call you Youth in the high heavens?’ He answered and said to me, ‘Because I am Enoch son of Jared. When the generation of the Flood sinned and said to God, Depart from us; we do not desire knowledge of Your ways, the Holy One, blessed be He, took me up from among them to be a witness against them in the high heavens to all who come into the world, so that they should not say, The Merciful One is cruel! What sin did all those multitudes commit? And if they sinned, their wives, their sons and their daughters, their horses, their mules, their cattle and all their possessions, and all the birds in the world that the Holy One, blessed be He, destroyed with them in the days of the generation of the Flood — what sin did they commit, that they were swept away with them? Therefore He took me up in their lifetime, before their eyes, into the high heavens, to be a witness against them for the world to come; and the Holy One, blessed be He, assigned me on high as a prince and a ruler among the ministering angels.’

Uzza and Azael, of the ministering angels, were against me in the high heavens, and they said before the Holy One, blessed be He, ‘Master of the world, did not the first ones speak well before You: You shall not create man any more?’ (An allusion to the angels who accused at the creation of man and said, What is man that You should remember him? And see Yalkut Reuveni 23d, in the name of Hakham ha-Razim.) The Holy One, blessed be He, answered and said to them, ‘I have made, and I will bear; I will carry, and I will deliver.’ And when they saw me, they said before Him, ‘Master of the world, what is the nature of this one who has gone up to the height of heights? Is he not one of the sons of those who perished in the days of the Flood?’ Again the Holy One, blessed be He, answered and said to them, ‘What business is it of yours, that you come in to speak [rebelliously] about one in whom I delight more than in all of you, to be a prince and ruler over you in the high heavens?’ At once they all rose and went out to meet me and bowed down before me, and said to me, ‘Happy are you, and happy are your parents, for your Creator has favoured them.’ And because I am small among them and a youth among them in days, in months and in years, therefore they call me Youth. Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Prince of the Presence, said to me (ibid., folio 25b): From the day that the Holy One, blessed be He, drove out the first Adam from the Garden of Eden, the Shekhinah [the Divine Presence] dwelt upon a cherub under the Tree of Life; and the ministering angels would hasten and come and go down, band after band, from heaven to roam through the whole world; and the first Adam and Eve sat at the gate of the Garden of Eden to gaze on the likeness of the form of the radiance of the Shekhinah, for the radiance of the Shekhinah went from one end of the world to the other, three hundred and sixty-five thousand [times] the orb of the sun. For whoever gazed on the radiance of that Shekhinah, flies and gnats did not settle on him, and he did not fall ill, and no harmful spirits could harm him; and not only that, but angels had no power over him. And the Holy One, blessed be He, would go about and roam from the Garden to Eden and from Eden to the Garden, and from the Garden to the firmament and from the firmament to the Garden of Eden, and all gazed on the radiance of the likeness of His Shekhinah and were not harmed — until the people of the generation of Enosh came. They would go from one end of the world to the other, and each one of them would bring silver and gold, precious stones and pearls, in heaps like mountains upon mountains and hills upon hills, and make them into idols in the world to the measure of a thousand parasangs; and they brought down the sun and the moon, the stars and the constellations, to stand before them on their right and on their left, to attend on them in the way they attended on the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, All the host of heaven standing by Him on His right and on His left. And how did they have the power to bring them down and make use of them? Uzza and Azael taught them sorceries by which they brought them down and made use of them; for had it not been so, they could not have brought them down. At that hour the ministering angels raised an accusation before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said before Him, ‘Master of the world, what have You to do with human beings? What is man (enosh) that You should remember him? It does not say What is adam, but What is enosh, for he is the head of idolatry. Why did You leave the highest heavens of heavens, the abode of Your glory, and the high and exalted throne that is in the height of Aravot, and go among human beings who worship idols, who have made You equal to idols? Now You are on the earth and the idols are on the earth: what business have You among the dwellers on earth who worship idols?’ The Holy One, blessed be He, removed the Shekhinah from the earth, from among them. At that hour the ministering angels came, of the troops of the hosts and the armies of Aravot, a thousand myriads of hosts, and took the trumpets and grasped the horns in their hands, and surrounded the Shekhinah with songs and hymns [up] to the high heavens, as it is said, God has gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of the horn.

Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: When [the Holy One] sought to take me up on high, He first sent me Anafiel the prince, and he took me from among them before their eyes and conducted me in great glory on a chariot of fire, with horses of fire and ministers of glory, and took me up to the Shekhinah in the high heavens. And when I reached the high heavens, the holy creatures, the *ophanim*, the seraphim and the cherubim, the wheels of the chariot and the ministers of consuming fire smelt my smell at a distance of sixty-five thousand three hundred parasangs, and they said, ‘What is this smell of one born of woman, and what is this taste of a white drop, that he goes up into the high heavens and is to serve among the hewers of flame?’ The Holy One, blessed be He, answered and said to them, ‘My ministers, my hosts, my cherubim, my *ophanim* and my seraphim, let not your hearts be grieved at this, for all human beings denied Me and My great kingdom and went and worshipped idols, and I removed the Shekhinah from among them and went up on high. And this one whom I have taken from among them is the choicest of them all, and this one is equal to all of them in faith, in righteousness and in rightness of deed; and this one I have taken as My wage in My world under the heavens.’ (See Tziyyoni, folio 13d, and Yalkut Reuveni 24a.) Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: When they took me from among the people of the generation of the Flood, they lifted me on the wings of the wind of the Shekhinah to the uppermost firmament and brought me into the great palaces that are in the height of the firmament Aravot, where the throne of glory is, the Shekhinah and the chariot; and there are troops of fire and armies of fury, *shin'anim* [an angelic order] of wrath and cherubim of torch, *ophanim* of coal, ministers of flame, *hashmallim* [an angelic order] of flash and seraphim of lightning; and they stationed me to serve the throne of glory every single day. Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: Before they stationed me to serve the throne of glory, the Holy One, blessed be He, opened to me one thousand three hundred thousand gates of wisdom, three hundred thousand gates of understanding, three hundred thousand gates of prudence, three hundred thousand gates of life, three hundred thousand gates of peace, three hundred thousand gates of the Shekhinah, three hundred thousand gates of might and valour, three hundred thousand gates of strength, three hundred thousand gates of grace and loving-kindness, three hundred thousand gates of love, three hundred thousand gates of delight, three hundred thousand gates of humility and three hundred thousand gates of the fear of sin. At that hour the Holy One, blessed be He, added to me wisdom upon wisdom, understanding upon understanding, prudence upon prudence, knowledge upon knowledge, mercy upon mercy, Torah upon Torah, love upon love, loving-kindness upon loving-kindness, delight upon delight, humility upon humility, might upon might, strength upon strength, valour upon valour, brilliance upon brilliance, beauty upon beauty, comeliness upon comeliness; and I was honoured and glorified with all these good and praiseworthy qualities more than all the beings on high. Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: After all these qualities the Holy One, blessed be He, laid His hand on me and blessed me with three hundred and sixty-five thousand blessings; and I was raised up and made tall to the measure of the length and breadth of the world, and seventy-two wings were raised upon me, thirty-six wings on one side and thirty-six wings on the other, and each wing was like the fullness of the world; and He set in me three hundred and sixty-five thousand eyes, and each eye was like the great light; and He left no kind of radiance, comeliness, beauty or light in the world that He did not set in me. Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: All this the Holy One, blessed be He, did for me. He made me a throne like the throne of glory, and spread over me a canopy of radiance and brilliance, of comeliness, glory, beauty and grace, like the canopy of the throne of glory, with every kind of radiance of the lights in the world set in it; and He placed it at the entrance of the seventh palace and seated me on it. And the herald went out into every single firmament, saying: ‘Metatron My servant I have made prince and ruler over all the princes of My kingdom and over all the beings on high, except the eight princes, honoured and terrible, who are called LORD after My name, Prince of the World. And every angel who has a matter to speak before Me shall go before him and speak to him; and every word that he speaks to you in My name you shall keep and do; for the Prince of Wisdom and the Prince of Understanding serve him, to teach him the wisdom of the upper and the lower beings, the wisdom of this world and the secret of the world to come. And I have also appointed him over all the treasuries of the palace of Aravot and over all the stores of life that are in the high heavens.’ Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: The Holy One, blessed be He, revealed to me every kind of the hidden things of the Torah, all the mysteries of wisdom and all the depths of the perfect Torah, and all the thoughts of the hearts of creatures; and all the mysteries of the world and all the secrets of creation are revealed before me as they are revealed before the Maker of creation. And from then on I watched, to gaze into the mysteries of its depth and into its wondrous secret. Before a man thinks, I know; before he hides [a thing] in secret places, I see; before a man acts, I know; and there is nothing on high hidden from me or too deep for me.

Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: Out of the love with which the Holy One, blessed be He, loved me more than all the beings on high, He made me a garment of majesty in which every kind of light is set, and wrapped me in it; and He made me a royal crown in which are set forty-nine stones that burn with the light of the orb of the sun, whose radiance goes into the four [quarters of] the firmament Aravot, into the seven firmaments and into the four winds of the world; and He bound it on my head and called me the Lesser YHWH before all His household on high, as it is said, For My name is within him. Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: Out of the great love and great compassion with which the Holy One, blessed be He, loved and cherished me more than all the beings on high, He wrote with His finger, with a pen of flame, on the crown that is on my head, the letters by which heaven and earth were created, the letters by which seas and rivers were created, the letters by which mountains and hills were created, the letters by which stars and constellations, lightnings, wind and thunders, thunderclaps, snow, hail, storm and tempest were created, the letters by which the needs of the world and all the secrets of creation were created; and each and every letter shines, face to face, like the appearance of the going forth of the sun, and the moon and the stars. Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: When the Holy One, blessed be He, bound this crown on my head, all the princes of kingdoms in the height of Aravot and all the armies of every firmament trembled before me; and even the princes of the *elim* [mighty ones], the princes of the *tafsarim* [officers] and the princes of the *erelim* [an angelic order], who are greater than all the ministering angels who serve before the throne of glory, trembled and shook before me; and even Samael the wicked, the head of all the adversaries, who is great in all the kingdoms on high, feared and quaked; and even the angel of fire, the angel of hail, the angel of wind, the angel of lightning, the angel of wrath, the angel of thunder, the angel of snow, the angel of rain, the angel of the day, the angel of the night, the angel of the stars and the constellations, who guide the whole world by their hands, tremble and shake before me when they see me. And these are the names of the princes who guide the world: Gabriel, the angel of fire; Baradiel, the angel of hail; Ruhiel, the angel who is appointed over the wind; Barakiel, the angel who is appointed over the lightnings; Za'amiel, who is appointed over wrath; Zikiel, who is appointed over the sparks; Zu'iel, who is appointed over the tremors; Za'afiel, who is appointed over the raging storm; Ra'amiel, who is appointed over the thunders; Ra'ashiel, who is appointed over the earthquake; Shalgiel, who is appointed over the snow; Matariel, who is appointed over the rain; Shimshiel, who is appointed over the day; Leliel, who is appointed over the night; Galgalliel, who is appointed over the orb of the sun; Ofanniel, who is appointed over the wheel of the moon; Kokhaviel, who is appointed over the stars; Rahatiel, who is appointed over the constellations. And all of them fall on their faces when they see me, and cannot gaze at me because of the majesty and splendour, the radiance, brilliance, beauty, comeliness, brightness and light of glory that are on my head. Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, the splendour of the height of all, said to me: When the Holy One, blessed be He, took me to serve the throne of glory and the wheels of the chariot and all the needs of the Shekhinah, at once my flesh was turned to flame, my sinews to fire, my bones to coals of broom, the light of my eyelids to the brilliance of the firmament, the balls of my eyes to torches of fire, the hair of my head to blaze and flame, all my limbs to wings of burning fire, and the body of my stature to blazing fire. On my right are hewers of flames of fire, on my left a torch of fire burns, and around me blows a wind of tempest and storm, and the noise of quake upon quake, before me and behind me.

Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: Above them there is one prince, great and terrible, mighty and honoured, a chief and revered, venerable and strong, and Afafniel YHWH is his name. He has sixteen faces, four on each side, and he has eight thousand seven hundred and sixty-four eyes, according to the number of the hours of the days of the year, two thousand one hundred and ninety-one (four times 2,191 comes to 8,764; see Hekhalot, chapter 2), and sixteen on each side. And in those two eyes that are in his face, in each one lightnings flash and in each one torches burn, and no creature can gaze at them, for whoever gazes at them is burned up at once. And the height of his stature is a journey of two thousand five hundred years, which no creature's eye can see and no mouth can tell, nor the might of his strength, but only the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, alone. And why is his name called Afafniel? Because he is appointed over the *ophanim* [wheels], and they are given into his hand; and he stands every day and serves them and awes them and adorns them, and orders and arranges their running, and assembles their platform, and makes their dwelling pleasant, and waters their corner, and enriches their seat; and he attends on them early and late, night and day, to increase their beauty and magnify their majesty and make them swift in the praise of their Creator. And the *ophanim* are all full of eyes and full of wings, eyes facing wings and wings facing eyes, and from among them shines a light like the light of Venus; and seventy-two sapphire stones are set on the crown of each one of them, whose radiance goes into the four quarters of Aravot, [like] the orb of the sun whose radiance goes into the four quarters of the world. And why is his name called Zadkael? Because his radiance resembles the appearance of Tzedek [the planet Jupiter]; and booths of radiance surround them, booths of brilliance, booths of the light of sapphire and emerald, because of the appearance of the likeness of eyes.

Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: Above them there is one prince, wondrous and glorious, precious, mighty and fearsome, a chief and a leader, splendid, honoured and lovely; he is all full of radiance, all full of praise and brightness, all full of brilliance, all full of light, all full of beauty, of great loveliness. His likeness is like angels and his body like eagles; his radiance is like lightnings, his form like torches, his beauty like flashes, his majesty like streams, his splendour like *hashmallim* [an angelic order], his brightness like the light of Venus, his appearance like the great light, his height like the seven firmaments, and the light of his eyelids like the sevenfold light. And the sapphire stone on his head is as [great as] the fullness of the world, like the radiance of the very heavens for clearness; and his body is full of eyes like the stars of heaven, beyond searching and without end, and every eye is like the planet Venus; and some of them are like the lesser light and some of them like the great light. From his ankles to his knees [he is] like stars of lightning, from his knees to his thighs like the stars of Venus, from his thighs to his loins like the light of the moon, from his loins to his neck like the light of the sun, and from his neck to the crown of his head like a light that never fails; and the crown on his head is like the radiance of the throne of glory. The measure of the crown is a journey of five hundred and two years, and there is no kind of radiance, no kind of brilliance, no kind of brightness and no kind of light in the world that is not set in that crown. And that prince, Serafiel YHWH is his name, because he is appointed over the seraphim, and the seraphim of flame are given into his hand; and he stands over them night and day and teaches them song and praise, glory, strength and majesty, to glorify their King with every kind of praise and holiness. And how many are the seraphim? Four, corresponding to the four winds of the world. And how many wings have they? Six, corresponding to the six days of creation. And how many faces have they? Sixteen faces, four to each direction. And the measure of the wings: each wing is like the fullness of the firmament. The measure of the faces: each face is like the face of the east, shining, each one like the radiance of the throne of glory, so that even the holy creatures, the *ophanim* of majesty and the cherubim of splendour cannot gaze at it, for whoever gazes at it, his eyes grow dim from the great radiance upon it. And why are they called seraphim? Because they burn (sorefin) the writing-tablets of Satan. Every day Satan sits with Samael the wicked, the prince of Rome, and with Damuel, the prince of Persia, and writes the iniquities of Israel on his tablets, and they give them to the seraphim to bring them in before the Holy One, blessed be He, to destroy Israel from the world. But the seraphim know plainly that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not wish this nation of the Holy One, blessed be He, Israel, to fall. What do the seraphim do? Every day they take them from Satan's hand and burn them in the blazing fire that is opposite the high and exalted throne, so that they do not come in before the Holy One, blessed be He, at the hour when He sits in judgment and judges the whole world as one. Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: Above the seraphim there is one prince, more exalted than all the princes, more wondrous than all the ministers, Dabriel YHWH is his name, who is appointed over the treasuries of His books. He takes out and brings in the book-chests, and he opens [them] and takes the books and gives them into the hands of the Holy One, blessed be He; and the Holy One, blessed be He, takes them from his hand and gives them before Him into the hands of the scribes, to read in the great court that is in the height of the firmament Aravot, before the household on high. And why is his name called Dabriel? Because from every single word (dibbur) an angel goes out, and stands in the choirs of the ministering angels, and they sing a song before Him when the time comes to say ‘Holy’.
